children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures moved lower during the week ended Nov. 4, as commodity funds liquidated long positions and the market took some direction from Chicago soybeans and soyoil.

Canola had held up reasonably well relative to soybeans and soyoil, but that strength was unsustainable and the bearish outside influence eventually weighed on values, said Tony Tryhuk, director of futures trading with RBC Dominion Securities in Winnipeg.
Tryhuk said commodity funds were "in charge," with the nearby technical signals suggesting they could continue to liquidate their long positions.
January canola settled at C$768.30 per ton on Nov. 4, it's lowest close in three months. Tryhuk placed the next downside target at the 200-day moving average around C$763 per ton.
He expected values could stabilize above that level, as farmer selling had slowed with the end of harvest while bargain-hunting from end users underneath the market also supportive.

While technical signals and activity in outside markets should continue to provide direction in the short term, the longer-term direction may be tied to demand from the biofuel sector, said analyst Bruce Burnett of Glacier FarmMedia.

"It's all about what the renewable fuel policy will be," said Burnett on the eve of the U.S. midterm elections. With the Democrats gaining control of the House and Senate, he expected it would be positive for renewable fuels.
